sentences.text: Libycosuchus was an extinct North African crocodyliform that lived on land rather than in water.
It belongs to the monotypic family Libycosuchidae and is classified within the parent group Eunotosuchia.
The holotype specimen — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered in the early 1910s by Richard Markgraf.
The type species L. brevirostris was named in 1914 and formally described in 1915.
The animal lived approximately 95 million years ago, with its time range estimated between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
Fossil remains of this creature have been found in the Bahariya Formation in Egypt.
Scientists debate whether Libycosuchus is possibly related to Notosuchus.
